reason: The cited evidence shows that a hierarchical ultrafine lamellar structure in AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA improves strength–ductility synergy via back-stress strengthening (E1, E2), but it does not describe the specific cold-rolling and annealing route proposed, nor does it provide any data on creep resistance or the claimed quantitative improvements.
premises: Severe cold rolling and multi-step annealing of AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA can produce a hierarchical ultrafine lamellar microstructure.
Refined lamellar spacing and increased interfacial density enhance dislocation storage and back-stress strengthening.
Back-stress strengthening simultaneously improves strength and ductility in heterogeneous lamellar EHEAs.
Increased interfacial density and refined structure mitigate room-temperature creep by reducing grain-boundary sliding.
The proposed processing yields >15% increase in yield strength, comparable or higher ductility, and reduced creep strain.
